QF.id: SIA Logic Model for Social Programs_7

question.text: Roshni Trust (education-for-disabled NPO) has the output: 'Braille textbooks distributed to visually impaired students.' As SIA, which combination of Indicator + MoV + Assumption is the MOST SMART and audit-ready for this output row in the LFM?

answer.text: Indicator: 'Many books given out'; MoV: 'Teachers will confirm'; Assumption: 'Project will work'
Indicator: 'Books'; MoV: 'Internal MIS only'; Assumption: 'Future is predictable'
Indicator: 'Books distributed'; MoV: 'Trust me'; Assumption: 'None needed'

Indicator: '10,000 Braille textbooks distributed to 2,500 students across 50 schools in Karnataka by 31 Dec 2025'; MoV: 'Distribution logs signed by school principals, cross-checked with independent beneficiary call-back survey of 10% sample'; Assumption: 'Schools remain operational; Braille printing vendor delivers on schedule'

explanation.text: The Logic: Per the workbook's SMART discipline (page 93) and its LFM template guidance on indicators, means of verification and assumptions (pages 99-101), a sound output row needs Specific numbers, a Measurable target, an Achievable scope, a Relevant deliverable and a Time-bound deadline, all backed by objectively verifiable MoV and plausible external assumptions. Option D provides a quantified, time-bound indicator (10,000 books / 2,500 students / 50 schools / by 31 Dec 2025), dual-source MoV (signed distribution logs plus an independent beneficiary call-back survey) and external assumptions that the SIA can test. The Trap: Options A, B and C are vague, non-SMART or lack any verifiable MoV. They look like the kind of language that appears in poorly drafted SE project documents and must be rejected as audit-ready under the workbook's criteria. Note: The keyed answer is option D, which is the row that satisfies SMART and dual-source MoV; A, B and C each fail one or more of the SMART or MoV requirements.
